newsitem.title: USA: Cargo operators list airports wish lists.
newsitem.headline: Cargo operators list airports wish lists.

text.p: Airports have to start thinking like business partners and better serve their cargo airlines, executives told a conference here this week.
"Airport authorities have to have a business attitude, not a landlord attitude," Angelo Pusateri, New York-based, president- cargo for Virgin Atlantic Airways told the group.

Pusateri and other speakers had a range of suggestions for airports. Pusateri suggested such nut-and-bolts ideas as putting up better signs and eliminating toll roads near airports to ease traffic congestion so cargo can get to the airport more easily.
The conference brought together airport executives and air cargo executives, prompting both camps to discuss how they can work together for more profitable business for all.
The speakers said that not all cargo operators want the same services.

For example, traditional heavy freight haulers need plenty of warehouse space. But others such as some of the integrators, such as United Parcel Service, do not need big buildings at every airport because their sorting has been done at major hubs.
"We need fairly small buildings compared to the amount of aircraft parking space we require," said Doug Kuelpman, vice president of UPS.
Pusateri also said airport operators should not restrict carriers from handling freight of other carriers. Many airports limit those rights.
"Airports should not restrict carriers from offering any cargo service that can be profitable for the airlines," he said.
The remarks prompted Dayton International Airport director Roy Williams to warn airports not to take a cookie cutter approach to dealing with cargo.
Williams said: "This is a reminder that our assumptions of how air cargo operations work are not always safe assumptions."

The conference was sponsored by Airports Council International-North America, Air Freight Association and American Association of Airport Executives. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
